questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of `<!doctype html>` at the start of a modern HTML document?

options.text: It imports the browser's default CSS.
It tells the browser to use standards mode for HTML.
It declares the page's character encoding.

questions.explanation: The doctype is a short declaration that selects standards mode; it is not an HTML element or a version-specific DTD in modern HTML.

questions.prompt: Which element is the root element containing the document's head and body?
questions.explanation: The `html` element is the document root. Its document-level children are `head` and `body`.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which are semantic HTML elements with built-in meaning for page structure or content?
questions.explanation: `main`, `nav`, and `article` communicate structural meaning. `span` is a generic phrasing container without that specific meaning.

questions.prompt: Match each document element to its usual role.
questions.explanation: The `html` element contains the document, `head` holds metadata and resource references, and `body` holds the page's content.

questions.prompt: In this snippet, which element represents the main page heading?
questions.explanation: `h1` marks a top-level heading in the page content. The `title` element belongs in the head and supplies the document title.

questions.prompt: What is the best reason to choose heading levels such as `h2` and `h3`?

options.text: To make text bold without CSS.
To choose the font size for each section.
To add indentation to nested paragraphs.
To express the document's heading hierarchy.

questions.explanation: Heading elements describe section hierarchy. CSS can change their appearance, but visual size alone should not determine which heading element to use.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements describe HTML void elements?

options.text: Void elements do not have end tags.
A void element can contain nested child elements.

questions.explanation: Elements such as `img`, `input`, and `br` have no end tag and cannot contain children.

questions.prompt: Which part of this snippet tells the browser where the link should go?
questions.explanation: The `href` attribute supplies the hyperlink destination. The anchor's text gives users a readable link label.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of an informative image's `alt` text?

options.text: To set the image's displayed width.
To provide a text alternative for the image's relevant information.
To show a caption under every image.
To force the image to load before the page.

questions.explanation: Alternative text communicates an informative image's purpose or relevant content when the image cannot be perceived. Decorative images generally use an empty `alt` value.

questions.prompt: Where is the page's primary language normally declared for assistive technology and language processing?
questions.explanation: A document-level `lang` attribute on `html` identifies the primary language; language changes within passages can be marked on those elements.

questions.prompt: Which attribute supplies the image resource in this snippet?
questions.explanation: `src` identifies the image resource. The `alt` attribute provides its text alternative.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements about HTML attributes are correct?

options.text: `class` is a global attribute available on HTML elements.
`id` identifies an element and should be unique within the document.
`disabled` is a boolean attribute; its presence enables the disabled state.
Every attribute must have a non-empty quoted value.

questions.explanation: `class` and `id` are global attributes. Boolean attributes are true when present; not every HTML attribute is required to have a value.

questions.prompt: Match each list element to the list it represents.
questions.explanation: `ul` represents an unordered list, `ol` an ordered list, and `dl` a description list of terms and descriptions.

questions.prompt: Which element contains the items in this unordered list?
questions.explanation: List items are represented by `li` elements nested inside `ul` or `ol`.

questions.prompt: How does a relative URL such as `images/logo.png` differ from an absolute URL?

options.text: It always names a different website.
It is resolved relative to a base URL, commonly the current document URL.
It cannot be used in an `img` element.

questions.explanation: A relative reference is resolved against a base URL. An absolute URL includes the information needed to identify its resource independently.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements about hyperlinks are correct?

options.text: An `a` element with `href` creates a hyperlink.
A fragment such as `#details` can point to an element with that ID.
An anchor with no `href` is automatically a link to the current page.
`href` can contain a web URL or a supported URL scheme such as `mailto:`.

questions.explanation: Anchors become hyperlinks through `href`; destinations may be URLs, fragments, or supported schemes. An anchor without `href` is not a hyperlink.

questions.prompt: What does `target="_blank"` request for a link?

options.text: It opens the destination in a new browsing context, commonly a tab.
It opens the destination inside the current page's `head`.

questions.explanation: `_blank` requests a new browsing context; browser settings determine whether that appears as a tab or window. For external links, use the site's recommended `rel` values as well.

questions.prompt: Which element names a term in the description list shown here?
questions.explanation: `dt` marks a term or name, and `dd` provides its description or value inside a `dl`.

questions.prompt: Which table element represents a header cell?
questions.explanation: `th` represents a header cell. `td` represents data cells; `thead` groups header rows, and `caption` names the table.

questions.prompt: What does the `scope` attribute on a table header cell help identify?

options.text: The URL for the table data
Whether the header applies to a row or column

questions.explanation: Values such as `row` and `col` describe the direction in which a `th` applies, helping establish table header relationships.

questions.prompt: Which form attribute specifies the URL that receives a submitted form?
questions.explanation: `action` specifies the submission destination. `method` selects how the form data is sent.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which are valid ways to associate a visible label with an input?

options.text: Set a label's `for` value to the input's `id`.
Place the input inside its `label` element.
Set the label's `for` value to the input's `name`.
Use placeholder text instead of a label.

questions.explanation: A label can explicitly reference an input's unique `id` with `for`, or contain the input. Placeholder text is not a substitute for a persistent label.

questions.prompt: Inside a form, what is the default type of a `<button>` with no `type` attribute?
questions.explanation: A button associated with a form defaults to submit behavior. Use `type="button"` for a button that should not submit the form.

questions.prompt: Which attribute gives a form control its key in the submitted name/value data?
questions.explanation: The control's `name` is used as the submitted field name. Controls without a name are generally omitted from form submission.

questions.prompt: What does this form snippet provide?

options.text: A label associated with an input whose submitted name is `email`
A label explicitly associated with the input whose ID is `email`
An input that is required and read-only

questions.explanation: The label's `for="email"` matches the input's `id="email"`. A separate `name` is needed for a submitted field key.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements distinguish checkboxes from radio buttons?

options.text: Checkboxes can represent independently selectable choices.
Radio buttons with the same name form a group in which one choice is selected at a time.
A group of checkboxes can submit multiple selected values under a shared name.
Radio buttons are only valid outside forms.

questions.explanation: Checkboxes support independent selections; same-named radio controls form a single-choice group. Both control types can be used in forms.

questions.prompt: What does adding `required` to a supported form control do?

options.text: It guarantees the server will accept the value.
It hides the control until the form is submitted.
It asks the browser to require a value before normal submission.

questions.explanation: `required` participates in browser constraint validation. The server must still validate submitted data because client-side checks can be bypassed.

questions.prompt: When a selected `<option>` is submitted in a form, which value is sent?

options.text: Always the option's position in the list
The option's `value`, or its text when no value is provided

questions.explanation: A selected option contributes its `value`; when that attribute is omitted, its text content supplies the value.

questions.prompt: For an explicit label association, which attribute on the input must match the label's `for` value?
questions.explanation: The `for` attribute references the labeled control by its `id`. The `name` serves a different purpose in form submission.

questions.prompt: Which statement about forms is correct?

options.text: Forms can be nested to create separate submit regions.
A form must not contain another form element.
A form can contain only text inputs.
A form submits every element on the page.

questions.explanation: Nested forms are invalid HTML and have confusing parser behavior. Use separate forms or another appropriate interaction pattern.

questions.prompt: Which element is intended to identify the dominant, unique content of a page?
questions.explanation: `main` identifies the dominant content of the document. A page should ordinarily have one visible `main` landmark.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which choices use native HTML semantics appropriately?

options.text: Use a `button` for an action such as opening a dialog.
Use an `a` element with `href` for navigation.
Prefer native interactive elements over a clickable `div` when they fit the task.
Use `div` for every link because it automatically supports keyboard activation.

questions.explanation: Native buttons and links provide expected roles, focus behavior, and keyboard interaction. A generic `div` does not become an accessible control simply by looking clickable.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between `figure` and `figcaption`?

options.text: `figcaption` is a page-level footer for all figures.
`figure` can group self-contained content with an associated caption.
`figure` is only valid inside a table.

questions.explanation: `figure` groups self-contained content, often an illustration, and may contain a `figcaption`. A caption does not replace an image's text alternative.

questions.prompt: Match each table element to its role.
questions.explanation: `th` marks a header cell, `td` a data cell, and `caption` gives the table a title or description.

questions.prompt: What meaning does `strong` generally communicate?
questions.explanation: `strong` marks content with strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Its default bold appearance is not the reason to choose it.

questions.prompt: What meaning does `em` generally communicate?
questions.explanation: `em` marks stress emphasis that can affect sentence meaning. Use it for meaning, not merely to request italic styling.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which practices support accessible HTML content?

options.text: Provide a programmatically associated label for each form control.
Use meaningful alternative text for informative images.
Do not communicate important differences through color alone.
Use placeholder text as the only label for every input.

questions.explanation: Labels, useful image alternatives, and cues beyond color help users perceive and operate content. Placeholder text is not a persistent label.

questions.prompt: When is `aria-label` most appropriate?

options.text: To replace every visible heading on a page.
To make any element keyboard-operable without further work.
To provide an accessible name when a suitable visible label is unavailable.

questions.explanation: `aria-label` can provide an accessible name when a visible label is unavailable or unsuitable. Prefer native semantics and visible labels when possible.

questions.prompt: What character does this HTML character reference display as text?
questions.explanation: The named character reference `<` displays a literal less-than sign, which otherwise begins an HTML tag in markup.

questions.prompt: Where does the document's `title` element belong?
questions.explanation: The document `title` belongs in `head`. Browsers commonly display it in the tab or window title, and it helps identify the page.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements about common document metadata are correct?

options.text: `meta charset="utf-8"` declares the document's character encoding.
The `title` element identifies the document in browser interfaces.
A viewport meta declaration helps mobile browsers size and scale the layout viewport.
`meta name="keywords"` is required for modern search indexing.

questions.explanation: Character encoding, document title, and viewport metadata serve practical browser functions. The keywords meta tag is not required for modern search indexing.

questions.prompt: Match each form attribute to its primary purpose.
questions.explanation: The form's `action` specifies a destination, its `method` chooses GET or POST behavior, and each successful control's `name` identifies its submitted field.
